corpus.lang: Keko giduti-duti lon katokunu gisipi-sipiso kake.

toEnglish.explanation: S V O order. loke-loke = PL~sheepdog; kato-nu = wake-3PL; tima = huge; sipi-sipi-so = PL~shepherd-ACC; kake = at.dawn.

toLang.prompt: The hen does not wake a golden sheepdog.
toLang.explanation: S V O order. gi-duti = DEF-hen; lon = NEG; kato = wake; keko = golden; loke-so = sheepdog-ACC.

grammar: Word order: subject, verb, object. With one participant: subject, verb.
Plural: say the noun twice (tasige → gitasige-tasige).
Definite (“the”). A noun without it means “a” (or plain plural).
Past tense. Without it the verb is present or future.
On the verb when the subject is plural.
Negation: a separate word before the verb.
Come before the noun. Noun endings go on the noun only; the adjective stays bare.
Go at the end of the sentence.
